trajectory_summary: The call opens cold with visible call fatigue, recovers through an extended and genuinely warm rapport stretch, but that warmth is never converted into a booked appointment — the call ends on a personal joke and a vague promise to text, with no day/time offered. Energy was built with the customer but not channeled into the setter's actual job.
outcome_dispute: The call should be tagged no_appointment (or callback at best) rather than any booked/tentative outcome — no date or time is ever proposed by the rep; the closing exchange is purely about how the bill photo will be sent, and the call ends with 'we will keep in touch,' not a scheduled slot.

key_moments.quote: I've got your address here, Mike, as, 733 Ohio Dash 380.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep spends nearly two minutes (00:43-02:23) failing to confirm a basic address, cycling through wrong guesses (Ohio Dash 380, State Route 380, Moore's Body Shop) before the customer volunteers his actual address unprompted. This is a data-quality/CRM issue surfacing as call friction, not a rep skill failure per se, but it burns time and signals disorganization early.

The rep used it only for rapport, not as a bill-usage lead-in.
